facts.why: In the script McClane checks the floors and mutters '32 construction... 33 computers'. Floor 33 is the computer floor, not a building site.

facts.text: Long flight? Shoes off, stretch the legs, then grab a drink.
facts.why: The tip comes from a salesman seated next to McClane on the plane: take off your shoes and socks, walk around barefoot and make fists with your toes. Nothing I opened says he sat in 4B or mentions a drink.
facts.fix: Long flight? Shoes and socks off, make fists with your toes.

fix_note.text: Long flight? Shoes and socks off, make fists with your toes.

facts.text: Same recipe as the back of the limo.
facts.why: Argyle lists the limo's extras as CD, CB, TV, VHS, telephone and full bar. None of the sources mention nuts or snacks in the back.
facts.fix: Pairs well with the full bar in the back of the limo.

facts.why: Wikipedia calls Holly a high ranking Nakatomi executive. The script gives Ellis the V.P. of Sales title and Takagi the Sr V.P. of Sales, but gives Holly no title.
Wikipedia calls Takagi Nakatomi's head executive, and the script calls him Sr V.P. of Sales. Neither source says president.
facts.fix: FROM THE HEAD OF THE COMPANY

vibe.verdict: A clean Nakatomi party menu that gets the building and the night right. It misses the best Die Hard jokes, and a couple of titles are off.
missing: Fists with your toes on the plane (the salesman)
Hans Gruber's fake American accent (the stairwell)
Ho ho ho on the dead man's shirt
The mimosa champagne punch at the party
ideas: Fix the floors sign to '32 construction, 33 computers'
Swap the 4B tip for the salesman's fists with your toes line
Replace the 'Champagne by the bottle, Ellis picks' line with 'Mimosa champagne punch, watered down'
Swap 'Christmas Sugar Cookies' note for a Twinkies joke from the 7-Eleven
